notice: Fictional bank rows for measuring the cost classifier. No row comes from a real statement or a real person. People, small local providers, schools and employers are made up, and a match with a real one is a coincidence; account numbers and IDs are invented and phone numbers use the 555 range. Real companies and public agencies appear only as the name a bank would print. Written on Nov 16, 2026 by an AI assistant from how banks print descriptors. The assistant had read the classifier's rules before writing, so the rows are held out from the rules in time, not written blind. Every label in expect is proposed and has not been checked by a person. The rows were committed before the classifier was first run on them and are not to be edited to change a result; corrections go in classifier-heldout.reviewed.csv.
label_policy: The label is the kind of expense a careful person would name from the row, read with the other rows on the same statement. When the row cannot tell, the label is unknown, which means no cost label.
A bare pharmacy chain, general store, hardware store or electronics store row is unknown. A pharmacy counter, a mail-order pharmacy, or a row that names a prescription is prescription.

A store that sells only clothing is clothing_bedding, and a hotel is temporary_housing, whether or not the crime caused the purchase: the person confirms that part later. These labels are marked unsure in the note.
A ride, a fare or parking is transportation only when the statement shows an in-person care visit on the same date. On any other day it is unknown. Gas, food delivery and car rental are unknown.
A deposit, application fee, mover or truck is relocation. Ongoing rent, regular utility bills and insurance premiums are unknown. Student loan payments are unknown; a tuition payment plan is tuition.

A charge of a cost kind dated before the incident date is unknown, apart from tuition for the term the incident fell in. The classifier does not look at dates (a later step, the law engine, leaves out anything before the date), so the report counts these mistakes on their own line. A purchase that was refunded in full is unknown.
Money in is unknown, apart from a paycheck that came in clearly short on or after the incident date, which is lost_wages.
A note that starts with unsure marks a label the writer was not sure of. Those are the first rows to check.
